2d.name: First slide
2d.description: Slide the top square along its two neighbours.

2d.name: Around the corner
2d.description: Rotate the end square around its neighbour.

2d.name: Stand up
2d.description: Turn the horizontal chain into a vertical one.

2d.name: Cross to corner
2d.description: Fold the cross into an L. Watch the centre square: it holds the others together.

2d.name: Holding together
2d.description: Straighten the plus into a line. A square that holds the others together cannot move.

2d.name: Staircase
2d.description: Fold the staircase into a corner.

2d.name: Fill the hole
2d.description: Turn the ring around a hole into a solid block.

2d.name: Comb
2d.description: Gather the teeth of the comb into a diamond.

2d.name: Spiral
2d.description: Unwind the spiral into a block.

2d.name: Two rooms
2d.description: Two holes, two cycles: flatten them into a long block.

3d.name: Drop it
3d.description: Slide the top cube down into the corner.

3d.name: Under the arch
3d.description: Fill the gap under the arch.

3d.name: Pillar
3d.description: Bring the pillar down towards the corner.

3d.name: Paper [a]: Lower the head
3d.description: The tall pillar is on the right in this mirrored example. Its top cube rotates around the cube below it and lands one level lower on the left.

3d.name: Paper [c]: Unlock, then slide the base down
3d.description: The top cube of the left pillar slides right first. With the head supported by the right pillar, the base of the left pillar can slide down.

3d.name: Two layers
3d.description: Compact both layers into the corner. A cube may step just outside the box, but only one at a time.

3d.name: Paper [c]: Slide the base down
3d.description: The left pillar starts higher than the right one. Its lowest cube slides straight down along the right pillar.

3d.name: Paper [d]: Unlock, then rotate the base down
3d.description: The top cube slides right to unlock the left pillar. Then the left base rotates around the right base into the empty floor cell.

3d.name: Spatial staircase
3d.description: A staircase climbing in all three directions.

3d.name: Tower
3d.description: A tall pillar in the far corner: bring it down.

3d.name: Paper [d]: Rotate the base down
3d.description: Both front pillars start one cube above the floor. The left base rotates around the right base into the empty cell below it. The cubes behind provide floor support.

3d.name: Bridge
3d.description: Two feet joined by a fragile bridge.

3d.name: Paper [b]: Unlock, open a gap, then lower
3d.description: The top cube slides right first. This unlocks the left pillar, so a lower cube can slide right and the cube above it can drop into the gap.

3d.name: Corner pillars
3d.description: Pillars on two sides of the box.

3d.name: Scattered
3d.description: A winding path through all three dimensions.

3d.name: Paper [b]: Open a gap, then lower
3d.description: Watch the two front pillars. A cube slides right to open a gap in the left pillar, then the cube above slides down into it. The cubes behind the pillars keep them connected.

3d.name: Thin bridge · paper [e]
3d.description: Compare with Figure 3 [e] (p. 806). Either nine-cube leg can be shoved toward the middle column, but every other side of the source leg is outside the original box. The illustrated zipper parks two cubes on that helper side at once. The website solver uses the short shove here.

3d.name: Thin bridge · second shove
3d.description: Run without fallbacks to see the first leg move inward. Compare the remaining leg with Figure 3 [e] (p. 806) and look for a free helper column.

3d.name: Zipper
3d.description: Two tall legs joined at the top: the solver shoves each leg with the paper's zipper.
